translation_en: Abu Bakr ibn Nafi‘ narrated it to me: Ghundar narrated to us; Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated it to us: Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to us; and ‘Abd al-Warith ibn ‘Abd al-Samad narrated it to us: my father narrated to us. All reported from Shu‘bah with this chain. In Ghundar’s and Wahb’s reports it says, “He forbade”; in ‘Abd al-Samad’s report it says, “The Messenger of Allah forbade,” with a report like Mu‘adh’s from Shu‘bah.
Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: I recited to Malik, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, that the Messenger of Allah forbade deceptive bidding.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Ibn Abi Za’idah narrated to us; Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Yahya, meaning Ibn Sa‘id, narrated to us; and Ibn Numayr narrated to us: my father narrated to us. All reported from ‘Ubayd Allah, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, that the Messenger of Allah forbade intercepting goods before they reached the markets. This is Ibn Numayr’s wording. The other two said the Prophet forbade interception.
Muhammad ibn Hatim and Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated it to me, both from Ibn Mahdi, from Malik, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, from the Prophet, with a report like Ibn Numayr’s from ‘Ubayd Allah.
Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from al-Taymi, from Abu ‘Uthman, from ‘Abd Allah, from the Prophet, that he forbade intercepting sales.
Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: Hushaym informed us, from Hisham, from Ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah forbade intercepting incoming goods.

Ibn Abi ‘Umar narrated to us: Hisham ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who informed me that Hisham al-Qurdusi heard Ibn Sirin say: I heard Abu Hurayrah say that the Messenger of Allah said: “Do not intercept incoming goods. Whoever intercepts them and buys from them, when their owner reaches the market, he has the choice.”

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, ‘Amr al-Naqid, and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, attributing it to the Prophet, who said: “A city-dweller must not sell on behalf of a Bedouin.” Zuhayr’s narration says the Prophet forbade a city-dweller from selling on behalf of a Bedouin.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim and ‘Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us: ‘Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma‘mar informed us, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah forbade intercepting traders and a city-dweller selling on behalf of a Bedouin. I asked Ibn ‘Abbas what that meant, and he said, “He must not act as his broker.”

Yahya ibn Yahya al-Tamimi informed us: Abu Khaythamah narrated to us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir; and Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to us: Zuhayr narrated to us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said the Messenger of Allah said: “A city-dweller must not sell on behalf of a Bedouin. Leave people so that Allah may provide for some through others.” Yahya’s narration says “may be provided for.”
Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and ‘Amr al-Naqid narrated to us: Sufyan ibn ‘Uyaynah narrated to us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, from the Prophet, with a report like it.

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: Hushaym informed us, from Yunus, from Ibn Sirin, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: We were forbidden for a city-dweller to sell on behalf of a Bedouin, even if he were his brother or father.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Ibn Abi ‘Adi narrated to us, from Ibn ‘Awn, from Muhammad, from Anas; and Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Mu‘adh narrated to us, from Ibn ‘Awn, from Muhammad, who said Anas ibn Malik said: We were forbidden for a city-dweller to sell on behalf of a Bedouin.

‘Abd Allah ibn Maslamah ibn Qa‘nab narrated to us: Dawud ibn Qays narrated to us, from Musa ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah, who said the Messenger of Allah said: “Whoever buys a milk-retaining she-goat should take it home and milk it. If satisfied with its milk, he may keep it; otherwise, he may return it along with a measure of dates.”

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id narrated to us: Ya‘qub, Ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman al-Qari, narrated to us, from Suhayl, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah said: “Whoever buys a milk-retaining sheep has the choice for three days: if he wishes, he keeps it; if he wishes, he returns it and returns with it a measure of dates.”

Muhammad ibn ‘Amr ibn Jablah ibn Abi Rawwad narrated to us: Abu ‘Amir, al-‘Aqadi, narrated to us: Qurrah narrated to us, from Muhammad, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, who said: “Whoever buys a milk-retaining sheep has the choice for three days. If he returns it, he must return with it a measure of food, not wheat.”

Ibn Abi ‘Umar narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Muhammad, from Abu Hurayrah, who said the Messenger of Allah said: “Whoever buys a milk-retaining sheep has the better of two choices: if he wishes, he keeps it; if he wishes, he returns it along with a measure of dates, not wheat.”
Ibn Abi ‘Umar narrated it to us: ‘Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, from Ayyub, with this chain, except that he said: “Whoever buys livestock has the choice.”

Muhammad ibn Rafi‘ narrated to us: ‘Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma‘mar narrated to us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: These are reports Abu Hurayrah narrated to us from the Messenger of Allah. Among them he said the Messenger of Allah said: “If one of you buys a milk-retaining she-camel or sheep, he has the choice after milking it: if he keeps it, fine; otherwise, let him return it along with a measure of dates.”

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us; and Abu al-Rabi‘ al-‘Ataki and Qutaybah narrated to us: Hammad narrated to us, from ‘Amr ibn Dinar, from Tawus, from Ibn ‘Abbas, that the Messenger of Allah said: “Whoever buys food must not sell it until he has received it.” Ibn ‘Abbas said: I think everything is like that.

Ibn Abi ‘Umar and Ahmad ibn ‘Abdah narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us; Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Waki‘ narrated to us, from Sufyan al-Thawri. Both reported from ‘Amr ibn Dinar with this chain and a report like it.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, Muhammad ibn Rafi‘, and ‘Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us. Ibn Rafi‘ said: He narrated to us; the other two said: ‘Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma‘mar informed us, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said the Messenger of Allah said: “Whoever buys food must not sell it until he takes possession of it.” Ibn ‘Abbas said: I think everything is like food.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu Kurayb, and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us. Ishaq said: He informed us; the other two said: Waki‘ narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said the Messenger of Allah said: “Whoever buys food must not sell it until he measures it.” I asked Ibn ‘Abbas why. He said, “Do you not see that people trade for gold while the food is still deferred?” Abu Kurayb did not say “deferred.”

‘Abd Allah ibn Maslamah al-Qa‘nabi narrated to us: Malik narrated to us; and Yahya ibn Yahya said: I recited to Malik, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, that the Messenger of Allah said: “Whoever buys food must not sell it until he has received it.”

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: ‘Ali ibn Mushir narrated to us, from ‘Ubayd Allah; and Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn Numayr narrated to us—and the wording is his—my father narrated to us, from ‘Ubayd Allah, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, that the Messenger of Allah said: “Whoever buys food must not sell it until he has received it.” They used to buy food from caravans in bulk, so the Messenger of Allah forbade them from selling it until they moved it from its place.

Harmalah ibn Yahya informed us: ‘Abd Allah ibn Wahb narrated to us: ‘Umar ibn Muhammad narrated to me, from Nafi‘, from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar, that the Messenger of Allah said: “Whoever buys food must not sell it until he has received it and taken possession of it.”

Yahya ibn Yahya and ‘Ali ibn Hujr narrated to us. Yahya said: Isma‘il ibn Ja‘far informed us; ‘Ali said: Isma‘il narrated to us, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Dinar, who heard Ibn ‘Umar say the Messenger of Allah said: “Whoever buys food must not sell it until he takes possession of it.”

Yahya ibn Yahya said: I recited to Malik, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, who said: In the time of the Messenger of Allah, we would buy food, and he would send someone to order us to move it from the place where we bought it to another place before selling it.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: ‘Abd al-A‘la narrated to us, from Ma‘mar, from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from Ibn ‘Umar, that in the time of the Messenger of Allah people who bought food in bulk were beaten if they sold it where they bought it before moving it.

Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me: Ibn Wahb narrated to us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, who informed me that Salim ibn ‘Abd Allah said his father said: I saw people in the Messenger of Allah’s time who bought food in bulk being beaten if they sold it where they had bought it, until they brought it to their loads. Ibn Shihab said: ‘Ubayd Allah ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar told me that his father used to buy food in bulk and carry it to his family.
